sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 4.1, JAMS p.928, proof p.929; author p.13–14
sourceIssues.printed: "Theorem 4.1. Let V be a polarized variation of pure Hodge structures of weight k over the punctured polydisk (∆*)^n, with period map Φ: (∆*)^n → S_{Γ,G,M}. Then Φ is R_an,exp-definable." (∆ is the unit disk, p.4.)
sourceIssues.correction: Definability holds only after shrinking. For some radius 0 < ρ < 1, the restriction of Φ to (∆*_ρ)^n is R_an,exp-definable, and then for every ρ < 1 by compactness of the remaining annular pieces. The reduction in §4.1 must use charts whose shrunken polydisks still cover the compactification.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample (n = 1, trivial monodromy). Let f(z) = exp(−(1+z)/(1−z)) on the unit disk, so |f| < 1, and τ = 2i + εf with ε small, so that τ(∆) lies in a disk on which π: H → Γ\H is injective (Γ torsion-free, e.g. Γ(3)). τ is the period map of a polarized weight-one integral VHS. But Φ^{−1}(π(2i + ε/e)) contains the points z_n = 2πin/(2 + 2πin), n ≠ 0, where f = 1/e. These form an infinite discrete set accumulating at 1, which is impossible for a fibre of a definable map. The proof itself allows for this: it says 'after maybe shrinking the polydisk' (p.14), and its Siegel set S_H (y > 1) covers only |q| < e^{−2π}. Theorem 1.3 is unaffected, since §4.1 can use finitely many shrunken charts. Checked numerically: |f(z_n) − 1/e| < 1e−8 for 0 < |n| ≤ 2000. Noted by the extraction (item local-outer-boundary-obstruction). (cc-442dc5) Rechecked: the proof on p.929 says 'after maybe shrinking the polydisk', so the intended statement is the shrunken one, and §4.1 needs only finitely many shrunken charts; Theorem 1.3 is unaffected. The printed statement for the whole punctured polydisk is still false, so the finding keeps 'a stated result'.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 4.5 proof, JAMS p.930; author p.15
sourceIssues.printed: "Consider for each positive integer m and real number c the function f_{m,c} which we obtain from f by setting z_1 = mz_2 + c. Note that the assumptions of the lemma still apply to f_{m,c}, and it follows by induction on n that f_{m,c} ≪ 1 on all of Σ_{n−1}"
sourceIssues.correction: State the lemma, and verify its curve hypothesis, on wider sectors Σ_n^R={|x_i|<R,y₁≥⋯≥y_n>1} for every R, with constants depending on R. The substitution maps Σ_(n−1)^R′ into Σ_n^(mR′+|c|). The application needs original-source bounded-real-width uniformity for Schmid Corollary 5.29 and the CKS/Kashiwara norm estimates; G3 records that this is still unverified. The R-quantifier of the target Theorem 1.5 is not evidence for its prerequisites.
sourceIssues.reason: Σ_n is defined with 0 < x_i < 1 (Definition 4.4). The proof uses c = 0, 1, …, r_1 and m ≥ 1. For c ≥ 1, x_1 = mx_2 + c > 1, so Σ_n ∩ {z_1 = mz_2 + c} is empty. For c = 0 it is only the strip x_2 < 1/m. So the hypothesis gives no information about f_{m,c} on Σ_{n−1}. The functions extend there (the coefficients in O are periodic in x and f is polynomial in x), but the bound is assumed only on Σ_n. With the R-uniform hypothesis, the finite difference in c isolates the top x_1-degree, the Vandermonde step in m isolates each y-power, and |x_1| < 1 on Σ_n finishes the proof, as printed. Noted by the extraction (verification gap G4); the repair is given by this continuation.

sourceIssues.printed: "Moreover, if b is (e′, C′)-reduced and e is a basis for which condition (3) of Definition 4.11 holds for some C > 0, then b will also be (e, C″)-reduced for some C″ = C″(e, C, e′, C′) > 0."

sourceIssues.reason: Take e′ = (e_1, e_2), e = (e_2, e_1) and b = diag(1, T) with T ≥ 1. Then b is (e′, 2)-reduced and satisfies condition (3) for e (b(e_2)b(e_1) = T = det b), but condition (2) for e would need T = b(e_2) < C″b(e_1) = C″ for all T. The proof immediately adds 'we may assume (2) as there are only finitely many orderings of the basis', which is the corrected form, so Theorem 1.5 is unaffected. sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 1.1(1), JAMS p.919; Definition 2.5 and Proposition 2.7, p.924
sourceIssues.printed: "(1) The arithmetic quotient S_{Γ,G,M} := Γ\G/M admits a natural structure of R_alg-definable manifold, characterized by the following property. ... S ⊂ G/M a semi-algebraic Siegel set ..."
sourceIssues.correction: The definable structure depends on a choice of maximal compact subgroup K ⊃ M. For each such K there is a structure S_{Γ,G,M,K}, characterized by the Siegel sets associated to K. Definition 2.5 must fix K, and Proposition 2.7 holds when all Siegel sets use the same K (Erratum, Theorem 1.2(1)).
sourceIssues.reason: Erratum §1.6.1: for G = SL₂, a Siegel set built with K_x is not contained in finitely many Siegel sets built with K_i when x ≠ i, so the two structures on Γ\G differ. The Hodge-theoretic statements are unaffected, because Hodge manifolds carry a canonical K (Erratum §1.4).

sourceIssues.reason: Let G=SL₂(R), M=SO₂(R), W=Sym₂(R)⊕R with g·(A,t)=(gAgᵀ,t), v=(I,1). This line has stabilizer M. For g=diag(2,1/2) and k=[[0,−1],[1,0]]∈M, all M-invariant polynomials have equal values on g·v and kg·v. Yet gM≠kgM: the symmetric matrices diag(4,1/4) and diag(1/4,4) differ. Thus the proposed identification via p fails. This does not refute existence of a semialgebraic homogeneous quotient.

sourceIssues.locator: Appendix A.3 proof of Proposition A.2, JAMS pp.935–936
sourceIssues.correction: Choose smaller semialgebraic corner boxes whose closures lie inside larger analytic charts. Prove definability of the compact matching graph and cover it by finitely many neighborhoods of analytic transition extensions. Mere boundedness of the smaller domains is insufficient.
sourceIssues.reason: Analytic coordinate changes between relatively compact domains need not be R_an-definable: F(x)=x+(x²/4)sin(1/x), 0<x<1, has derivative greater than 1/4 and maps diffeomorphically to a bounded interval. If F were definable, the zero set of F(x)−x, containing exactly x=1/(nπ), n≥1, would contradict o-minimality. Reparametrize an analytic arc in a compact circle by F. Thus a buffer in larger charts is necessary for the printed immediate inference. The new buffered-transition-graph item supplies a proof of the theorem, not a counterexample to its conclusion.
